'''Melissa Bean''' (née '''Luburich'''; born January 22, 1962) is an American politician who served as the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representative]] for {{ushr|Illinois|8}} from 2005 to 2011. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], Bean is set to return to her old seat after winning the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois#District 8|2026 U.S. House election]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/house/6123751-melissa-bean-wins-house-seat/|last=Bhakta|first=Mira|title=Bean set to return to Capitol Hill after Illinois House victory|work=The Hill|date=November 3, 2026}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Bean grew up in a [[Serbian-American]] family in the [[Chicago suburbs]], where her adopted father was a machine belt factory owner.<ref name="wp">{{cite news|title=Melissa Bean|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/melissa-bean/gIQAdI0HAP_topic.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120927015420/http://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/melissa-bean/gIQAdI0HAP_topic.html|archive-date=2012-09-27|newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=November 16, 2013|date=July 25, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://history.house.gov/People/Detail/10405|title=BEAN, Melissa L.|access-date=February 6, 2026}}</ref> She attended [[Maine East High School]] before graduating from [[Oakton College|Oakton Community College]] with an associate degree in 1982 and from [[Roosevelt University]] in 2000 with a bachelor's degree. 

== Early career ==
Prior to her election to congress, Bean was president of a home-based business, Sales Resources Inc.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/elections/2004/candidates/21997/|title=Melissa Bean CV|work=[[The Washington Post]]|year=2004|access-date=March 15, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402125921/https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/elections/2004/candidates/21997/|archive-date=April 2, 2015}}</ref>

=== 2002 U.S. House campaign ===
In 2002, Bean was [[2002 United States House of Representatives elections#Illinois|defeated]] by 73-year-old 8th district [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Phil Crane]], who had held the seat for 33 years. However, Bean managed 43 percent of the vote, surprising observers from both parties, given that the national party offered almost no financial support to her campaign.<ref>{{cite news|date=October 10, 2004|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2004/10/10/gop-fears-party-woes-may-be-getting-to-crane/|title=GOP fears party woes may be getting to Crane|work=Chicago Tribune|access-date=February 7, 2026}}</ref>

=== 2004 U.S. House campaign ===
Bean rematched against Crane in [[2004 United States House of Representatives elections#Illinois|2004]]. This time, Bean raised almost as much money as Crane, mainly from small donors. In contrast, Crane received most of his donations from [[political action committee]]s. Despite Republican efforts to help Crane, Bean defeated him with 52 percent of the vote, a margin of roughly four percentage points. [[George W. Bush]] carried the district in the [[2004 U.S. presidential election|concurrently-held presidential election]] by 12 points.<ref name=":3">{{cite news|date=December 12, 2004|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2004/12/12/bitter-end-to-35-year-career/|title=Bitter end to 35-year career|work=Chicago Tribune|access-date=February 7, 2026}}</ref> When Bean took office on January 3, 2005, she became the first Democrat to represent the district since it was formed in 1935.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kestenbaum|first=Lawrence|url=https://politicalgraveyard.com/geo/IL/ofc/usrep.html|title=Illinois: U.S. Representatives|publisher=The Political Graveyard|access-date=July 12, 2010}}</ref>

==U.S. House of Representatives==
[[File:Melissa Bean in the Capitol.jpg|thumb|Bean speaking in the Capitol, 2010.]]
Bean was a member of the moderate [[Blue Dog Coalition]] and the pro-business [[New Democrat Coalition]]. She served on the [[U.S. House Committee on Small Business|Small Business]] and [[U.S. House Committee on Financial Services|Financial Services]] committees after being granted a waiver by Democratic leadership.<ref name="wp"/>

===Committee assignments===
*[[United States House Committee on Financial Services|Committee on Financial Services]]
**[[United States House Financial Services Subcommittee on Capital Markets, Insurance, and Government-Sponsored Enterprises|Subcommittee on Capital Markets, Insurance and Government Sponsored Enterprises]]
**[[United States House Financial Services Subcommittee on Financial Institutions and Consumer Credit|Subcommittee on Financial Institutions and Consumer Credit]]
*[[United States House Committee on Small Business|Committee on Small Business]]
**[[United States House Small Business Subcommittee on Finance and Tax|Subcommittee on Finance and Tax]]
**[[United States House Small Business Subcommittee on Contracting and Technology|Subcommittee on Contracting and Technology]]
**[[United States House Small Business Subcommittee on Regulations, Healthcare and Trade|Subcommittee on Regulations, Healthcare and Trade]]
===2010 defeat===
{{See also|2010 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois#District 8}}
Bean was challenged by Republican nominee [[Joe Walsh (American politician)|Joe Walsh]] and [[Illinois Green Party|Green Party]] nominee Bill Scheurer, an anti-[[Iraq war]] candidate.<ref name="fox"/><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.rrstar.com/elections/x1042479313/GOP-congressional-candidate-asked-to-drop-out|title=GOP congressional candidate asked to drop out|newspaper=Rockford Register Star|date=May 3, 2010|access-date=March 15, 2015}}</ref> Although Bean was heavily favored, she lost to Walsh by 291 votes.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.suntimes.com/news/elections/2900184,bean-concedes-tea-party-walsh-111710.article|title=Bean concedes 8th Cong. District seat to Tea Party's Walsh|work=Sun Times|date=November 16, 2010|access-date=March 15, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101120164429/http://www.suntimes.com/news/elections/2900184,bean-concedes-tea-party-walsh-111710.article|archive-date=November 20, 2010}}</ref> Bean was endorsed by the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'',<ref>{{cite news|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2010-10-07/news/ct-edit-congress-20101007_1_halvorson-adam-kinzinger-trillion-deficit|title=For the U.S. House|work=Chicago Tribune|date=October 7, 2010|access-date=October 9, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101108100847/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2010-10-07/news/ct-edit-congress-20101007_1_halvorson-adam-kinzinger-trillion-deficit|archive-date=November 8, 2010}}</ref> the ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'',<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.suntimes.com/news/elections/endorsements/2771554,CST-EDT-edit05b.article|title=Bean right for her district|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|date=October 5, 2010|access-date=October 9, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110614235109/http://www.suntimes.com/news/elections/endorsements/2771554,CST-EDT-edit05b.article|archive-date=June 14, 2011}}</ref> ''[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|The Daily Herald]]'',<ref>{{cite news|title=Congress, 8th District: Bean|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|date=October 16, 2010|url=https://www.dailyherald.com/article/20101016/discuss/710179931/|access-date=October 17, 2010}}</ref> and the ''[[Lake County News-Sun]]''.<ref>{{cite news|title=Our View: Bean, Seals for Congress|publisher=[[Lake County News-Sun]]|date=October 14, 2010|url=http://newssun.suntimes.com/opinions/1983552-474/news-district-congress-seals-business.html|access-date=October 17, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716163905/http://newssun.suntimes.com/opinions/1983552-474/news-district-congress-seals-business.html|archive-date=July 16, 2011}}</ref>

==Post-congressional career==
In 2011, Bean became President and CEO of the Executives Club of Chicago.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2011/03/01/melissa-bean-to-lead-executives-club-of-chicago/|work=Chicago Tribune|access-date=February 7, 2026|last=Yerak|first=Becky|title=Melissa Bean to lead Executives' Club of Chicago|date=March 1, 2011}}</ref><ref>[http://centennial.executivesclub.org/contact-us]  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130625131048/http://centennial.executivesclub.org/contact-us|date=June 25, 2013}}</ref> After serving as chair of Midwest operations for [[JPMorgan Chase]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/06/20/melissa-bean-jpmorgan_n_5515910.html|title=Former Congresswoman Now Officially Working For Wall Street|last1=Grim|first1=Ryan|last2=Carter|first2=Zachary D.|work=Huff Post|date=June 20, 2014|access-date=March 15, 2015}}</ref> she became CEO of Mesirow Wealth Advisors, part of [[Mesirow Financial]], in 2019.<ref>{{cite web|last=Marek|first=Lynne|url=https://www.chicagobusiness.com/finance-banking/mesirow-nabs-melissa-bean-jpmorgan|title=Mesirow nabs Melissa Bean from JPMorgan|work=[[Crain's Chicago Business]]|date=March 14, 2019|access-date=January 8, 2020}}</ref>

===2026 U.S. House campaign===
{{See also|2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Illinois#District 8}}
In September 2025, Bean announced her intention to run for her old congressional seat after a 15-year absence. The incumbent, five-term fellow Democrat [[Raja Krishnamoorthi]], was running for the [[2026 United States Senate election in Illinois|U.S. Senate]].<ref name=DH>{{cite news|url=https://www.dailyherald.com/20250911/news/melissa-bean-enters-8th-congressional-race-15-years-after-loss-to-joe-walsh/|last=Peterson|first=Eric|title=Melissa Bean enters 8th Congressional race, 15 years after loss to Joe Walsh|work=Daily Herald|date=September 11, 2025|access-date=February 7, 2026}}</ref> She was subsequently endorsed by [[Leading the Future]] super PAC backed by [[Andreessen Horowitz]] and [[OpenAI]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Kapos |first=Shia |date=February 11, 2026 |title=AI dollars boosting Jackson, Bean |url=https://www.politico.com/newsletters/illinois-playbook/2026/02/11/ai-dollars-flow-to-jackson-bean-00775556 |website=politico.com |location= |publisher=[[Politico]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260319002006/https://www.politico.com/newsletters/illinois-playbook/2026/02/11/ai-dollars-flow-to-jackson-bean-00775556 |archive-date=March 19, 2026 |access-date=May 26, 2026}}</ref> On March 17, 2026, Bean won the Democratic nomination after defeating candidates such as Junaid Ahmed- who was endorsed by prominent progressive lawmakers such as Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) and Sens. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.)- and Dan Tully.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wbez.org/government-politics/elections/2026/03/17/melissa-bean-wins-8th-congressional-district-primary-moves-to-reclaim-seat-she-lost-16-years-ago|title=Melissa Bean wins 8th Congressional District primary, moves to reclaim seat she lost 16 years ago|first1=David|last1=Struett|first2=Somer|last2=Van Benton|work=WBEZ Chicago|date=March 17, 2026|access-date=March 18, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/03/17/melissa-bean-wins-illinois-democratic-primary-house-00833516|title=AIPAC, AI money propels Melissa Bean to comeback victory in Illinois|first=Shia|last=Kapos|publisher=Politico|date=March 17, 2026|access-date=March 18, 2026}}</ref>

==Political positions==
===Tax cuts and finance===
In her first year in Congress in 2005, Bean was one of nine House Democrats to vote with Republicans to extend tax cuts on [[capital gains tax|capital gains]] and [[dividends]], a vote which [[House Democratic Leader]] [[Nancy Pelosi]] called "immoral".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Curry |first1=Tom |title=Why Democrats cross the aisle for a tax bill |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna10436531 |access-date=1 March 2026 |publisher=[[NBC News]] |date=12 December 2005}}</ref> She also departed from the Democrats in 2006 to vote to extend about $70 billion in the [[Bush tax cuts]]<ref name="fox">{{cite news|url=https://www.foxnews.com/story/gop-sees-opportunity-to-pick-up-seat-in-chicago-suburbs|title=GOP Sees Opportunity to Pick Up Seat in Chicago Suburbs|publisher=Fox News|date=August 20, 2006|access-date=March 15, 2015}}</ref> (she was one of just 15 Democrats to back the legislation). She also voted to [[repeal]] the estate tax<ref>{{cite news |last1=Walsh |first1=Thomas |title=Estate tax should not be repealed |url=https://www.dailyherald.com/20080130/opinion/estate-tax-should-not-be-repealed/ |access-date=1 March 2026 |work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]] |date=30 January 2008}}</ref> and voted in favor of a presidential [[line-item veto]] — votes that earned her the moniker "Tax Hero" from the anti-tax group [[Citizens Against Government Waste]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Moutevelis |first1=Alexa |title=Watchdog Group Names Rep. Bean a "Taxpayer Hero" Scores 80 Percent on CCAGW's Congressional Ratings |url=https://www.cagw.org/press/watchdog-group-names-rep-bean-a-taxpayer-hero-scores-80-percent-on-ccagws-congressional-ratings/ |access-date=1 March 2026 |publisher=[[Citizens Against Government Waste]] |date=10 July 2007}}</ref> Bean voted for the [[American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009]].

===Free trade===
Bean was one of only 15 Democrats to vote in favor of the [[Central American Free Trade Agreement]] (CAFTA),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cqpolitics.com/2006/07/il_8_freshman_bean_appears_str.html|title=Politics Home Page: Roll Call|access-date=October 28, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071022155942/http://cqpolitics.com/2006/07/il_8_freshman_bean_appears_str.html|archive-date=October 22, 2007}}</ref> a vote which lost her the endorsement of the [[AFL-CIO]] and other unions who viewed her vote as a betrayal, but gained her the support of — and awards from — the [[United States Chamber of Commerce]].<ref name="wp"/><ref name="fox"/> She co-sponsored the 2009 [[Employee Free Choice Act]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.opencongress.org/bill/111-h1409/show|title=H.R.1409: Employee Free Choice Act of 2009 - U.S. Congress|publisher=OpenCongress|date=March 10, 2009|access-date=July 12, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100723002539/http://www.opencongress.org/bill/111-h1409/show|archive-date=July 23, 2010}}</ref>, though it did not become law.

===Environment===
Bean supported the House Democratic [[cap-and-trade]] [[American Clean Energy and Security Act|bill]] in 2009, which would have capped carbon emissions from major U.S. sources and provided economic incentives for industries that reduce their emissions.<ref name="wp"/>
===Iraq war===
Bean supported the [[Iraq war]],<ref name="fox"/> but opposed President [[George W. Bush]]'s troop "surge" in 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.house.gov/apps/list/press/il08_bean/2152007_Iraq_War_Res.html|title=Bean Speaks in Support of Iraq War Resolution, in Opposition to Troop Surge|date=February 15, 2007|access-date=February 5, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100205101332/http://www.house.gov/apps/list/press/il08_bean/2152007_Iraq_War_Res.html|archive-date=February 5, 2010}}</ref> 
===Healthcare===
Bean supports [[pro-choice|abortion rights]] and voted in support of the [[Affordable Care Act]]. Bean was one of four Democrats to vote against the [[James Zadroga|James Zadroga 9/11 Health and Compensation Act of 2010]], joining 155 of 159 Republicans in defeating the bill.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2010/roll491.xml|title=H.R.847: James Zadroga 9/11 Health and Compensation Act of 2010 - U.S. Congress|date=July 29, 2010|access-date=August 18, 2010}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bean lives in unincorporated [[Palatine Township, Cook County, Illinois|Palatine Township]] with her husband and two girls.{{Update inline|date=March 2026|reason=Kids would likely be in their 30s by now...}} Their residence was in the 8th District when they moved there, but became part of the 10th District because of redistricting.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.c-spanvideo.org/program/164065-1|title=Illinois Redistricting Hearing &#124; Video &#124; C-SPAN.org|publisher=C-spanvideo.org|access-date=March 15, 2015}}</ref> Bean is [[Serbian Orthodox Church|Serbian Orthodox]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The Voter's Self Defense System|url=http://votesmart.org/|access-date=November 12, 2022|website=Vote Smart}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=109th Congress: Illinois|url=https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CDIR-2005-07-11/pdf/CDIR-2005-07-11-IL-H-8.pdf|date=July 11, 2005}}</ref>
